definitions.definition: Activity of body, speech and mind is inflow; auspicious activity brings merit, inauspicious demerit; with passions it is the lasting kind, without passions the transient; the lasting kind has the divisions of senses (5), passions (4), non-vows (5) and actions (25); the causes of the inflow of each karma type are given at 6.10-6.27.
Because of the passions the soul takes in material particles fit to become karma; that is bondage. Causes: wrong view, non-abstinence, carelessness, passions, activity.

Nature (prakṛti), duration (sthiti), intensity/fruition (anubhava) and quantity (pradeśa); nature is the eight karma types (8.4), duration is given for each (8.14-8.20), fruition is experiencing and follows the name (8.21-8.22), quantity concerns the particles in all the soul's space-points (8.24).
Knowledge-obscuring (5), perception-obscuring (9), feeling (2), deluding (28), lifespan (4), body-making (42), status (2), obstructive (5): ninety-seven subdivisions by this count.

name: The four passions and their sixteen varieties (Tattvārtha 8.9)

definitions.definition: Anger, pride, deceit and greed, each with four varieties: anantānubandhī, apratyākhyāna, pratyākhyāna, saṃjvalana; sixteen in all, forming the conduct-deluding karma of the passions.

name: The five states of the soul (Tattvārtha 2.1-2.7)

definitions.definition: Subsidential (2), destructional (9), mixed (18), rising (21, including four passions) and inherent (3): the soul's own nature (svatattva).

Five vows (abstention from violence, falsehood, stealing, unchastity, possessiveness), small or great; five contemplations for each; reflection on harm and suffering; friendliness, delight, compassion and equanimity; reflection on the nature of world and body for dread of saṃsāra and detachment.
Fruition is experiencing; it accords with the name of the karma; from it comes shedding (nirjarā).
